extracted.intended_audience: lawyers, adjudicators, policymakers and scholars working on Canadian social benefits appeals (CPP/QPP) and administrative procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes procedural and substantive standards governing appeals, review committees, the Pension Appeals Board (PAB), and the Umpire under the Canada Pension Plan (CPP) and Quebec Pension Plan (QPP). Focuses on duties, powers, time limits, evidence/records, impartiality, and procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural allowances for individuals (procedural fairness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the often disproportionate means at the disposal of the public authority and the individual, all procedural allowances must be made to the latter if he is to defend his interests adequately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle requires that individuals receive extra procedural assistance or allowances where necessary to ensure an adequate defence against a better-resourced public authority; applied throughout adjudicative and review proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data items to be recorded in PAB case files (sampling/record-keeping)
rubrics_metrics.description: We have extracted the following data from this sampling: file number, name and address of the individual concerned, place of the hearing, language used at the hearing, identity of the appellant, interventions, participation and representation of the parties at the hearing, nature and tenor of the contested decision, subject of litigation, dates of successive phases of the procedure, the decision of the PAB, caselaw cited, observations made by the PAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a model for what information should be contained in PAB records and for empirical study of PAB proceedings; implies comprehensive record-keeping for transparency and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspectors' powers under CPP sec.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The powers of these inspectors are regulated by sec. 26 of the CPP. They include right of access to the accounts of business firms and individuals, the right to examine accounts and documents and to require the cooperation of those having custody of the documents, the right to secure copies and, in the event of an apparent breach of the Act, to seize documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies scope of investigatory powers available to inspectors; relevant for assessing lawfulness of inspections and evidentiary procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for failing to provide required information (employers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 205 of the Regulations authorizes the imposition of a penalty not exceeding $250 on any employer failing to provide the required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational enforcement mechanism for noncompliance with information requests; useful in evaluating deterrence and compliance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minister's power to revise own decisions to take into account new facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister may, by virtue of sec. 86(2), revise his own decision so as to take into account new facts, even before he is requested to do so by the PAB: see M.H.W. v. Seigo (1972), CCH 6088.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes executive capacity to reopen and revise decisions in light of new information; affects timing of appeals and finality of initial determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to inform third parties of determinations once rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 28(7) authorizes the Minister to inform third parties concerned, not of his intention to render a determination, but of the determination itself, once it has been rendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits communication to the final determination (not pre-decisional intentions); relevant for privacy and procedural notice considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement and timing of medical reports for disability claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally, in strict compliance with the letter of the regulation, [the medical] report's submission was required at the time of the application for benefits. For some years now, however, the practice has been to dispense the applicant from the obligation of asking his physician for a report at the time of his application, and to rely on the applicant's own statements in the questionnaire concerning the essential facts in his case, subject to the additional confirmation provided by the subsequent medical report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice permits initial reliance on applicant questionnaires with subsequent medical confirmation; affects evidentiary expectations and applicants' burden at application time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to give notice of decisions (both positive and negative)
rubrics_metrics.description: CPP, sec. 59(3). The French version of this text (once again, an obvious mistranslation) suggests that the obligation to give notice of the decision only exists when the decision is negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correct rule requires notice of the decision (not only negative ones); watch for translation errors in bilingual texts that could misstate procedural obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic assessments of disability (sec.91(1)(j) and regs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 91(1)(j) of the CPP provides for 'periodic ... assessments' of the disability. CPP Regulations, sec. 532(1) and sec. 533 laid down by virtue of sec. 91(1)(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of disability are subject to ongoing reassessment; impacts duration and continuity of benefits and procedural follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'severe disability' for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'severe disability' in the meaning of sec. 43(2)a)(ii) of the CPP. CPP Regulations, sec. 535 and 536.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal threshold for benefit entitlement; essential for adjudicating disability claims and for evaluating claim sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable methods of application (telephone applications unacceptable)
rubrics_metrics.description: CPP, sec. 59(2); see M.H.W. v. McDermott (1976), CCH 6323, where an application made by telephone was held to be unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formal requirements for filing applications (written/formal submissions required); telephone filings may be invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for appeal and effect of reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: To recognize that a decision rendered on reconsideration, which merely confirms the initial decision, may be the subject of an appeal would be simply to make the time limit for appeal, laid down in sec. 83, meaningless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration that merely confirms the initial decision should not restart or nullify statutory appeal deadlines; protects finality and the operation of appeal time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chairman's power to summon parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chairman may notwithstanding summon the parties before him if he deems it useful; he has occasionally exercised this power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair has discretion to require attendance for clarification or fact-finding; supports active case management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality of Review Committee members and conflict-of-interest concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices of this kind illustrate what credence may be given to the postulate of impartiality in the case of all Committee members. See, for example: M.H.W. v. Durdle ... where the Chairman of the Committee as well as the appellant's appointed Committee member were both members of the provincial legislature. In Brooks v. M.H.W., the appellant unsuccessfully alleged that the Chairman had been appointed without the consent of the member designated by himself, and that he acted in a partial manner during the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality and appointment procedures are scrutinized by case law; appearance of bias and improper appointment procedures can ground complaints but may not always succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of interventions by the Umpire to avoid repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Umpire can order the consolidation of interventions raising the same questions of law or fact and originating with parties residing in the same region. This measure enables the parties to join their efforts in defence of their interests, and avoids the pointless repetition of identical testimony and pleas at the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case-management tool to increase efficiency and avoid duplicative evidence; supports regional consolidation where legal/factual overlap exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar duties and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The duties of the registrar of the Umpire are not laid down in any legal text. Section 2 of the Rules of Procedure simply defines the registrar as an official appointed by the Employment and Immigration Commission to administer the Umpire's office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar role is rule-defined rather than statutory; important for procedural administration though statutory duties may be absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for withdrawal of appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: A procedure for the withdrawal of appeals is provided under sec. 15 of Rules of Procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal process exists for withdrawal; withdrawn appeals may be liquidated by registrar (and were excluded from certain calculations in the authors' analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of Review Committee and PAB files beyond statutory time-limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The files of Review Committees are kept for this purpose by the PAB well beyond the time limit provided under sec. 23 of PAB Rules of Procedure (CPP benefits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice of extended record retention supports historical review and audits; indicates deviation from minimal statutory retention periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave and quorum requirements for QPP contributions appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: In the area of QPP contributions, leave must be given by the PAB, that is, by a quorum of three members, a provision which makes for considerable practical difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special procedural requirement (leave + three-member quorum) for QPP contributions appeals can create practical barriers and delays; relevant when planning appeal strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules governing hearings, representation, and procedures (PAB/Review Committee/Umpire Rules of Procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple provisions cited: Review Committee Rules of Procedure secs. 2–9, secs. 3(1), 4(1), 4(3), 5, 6, 7(1–3), 8(1–3), 9; PAB Rules of Procedure (CPP benefits) sec. 23, sec. 4–6, sec.10(1), sec. 11(1), sec. 19; Umpire Rules of Procedure secs. 2, 5–10, 12–24. These provisions govern matters such as composition, items of information, communication duties, hearings, consolidation, and powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective body of procedural rules that set out formal steps for appeals and hearings; each cited section must be consulted for precise procedural requirements and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and legal meaning of 'substantially' in benefits regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: QPP, sec. 105(?) and 226c); Regulations respecting benefits, sec. 6.01: 'substantially' means in a proportion higher than 50%. Consequently, it was required that the deceased contributor should have maintained himself entirely and should have contributed to the extent of 50% to the maintenance of his spouse, that is, should have contributed in the proportion of 75% to the maintenance of the household: Regime de rentes — 50, [1976] SAC 644.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies legal term 'substantially' (>50%) for entitlement calculations; important for assessing dependency and contribution proportions in benefit claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and appropriateness of occupational classifications (DOT / Descriptive Classification of Occupations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority used is the U.S. Dictionary of Occupational Titles, published by the U.S. Department of Labour. Although the work has been adapted for Canadian use by the federal Department of Manpower and Immigration, under the title of Descriptive Classification of Occupations, its appropriateness in the Canadian and Quebec context has been called in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupational classifications are used as evidentiary aids in assessing capacity/work history, but their cross-jurisdictional appropriation may be contested and should be scrutinized in Quebec/Canadian contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise of discretionary power in allocation of surviving spouse's pension
rubrics_metrics.description: The exercise of discretionary power is called for in the allocation of a surviving spouse's pension to the de facto spouse of a deceased contributor rather than to his legal spouse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretionary allocation requires individualized assessment and may implicate standards for fairness and evidence of relationship (cohabitation/support/public acknowledgement).
